perspective:
Harold’s available information:

- Harold is a project manager. He knows Arthur Begum as a friend and police officer whom he relies on for advice and support in stressful situations.
- Harold felt frustrated and anxious about his project’s progress and believed his team was not performing well due to a lack of motivation. He arranged a coffee-shop meeting with Arthur to ask for advice.
- Harold told Arthur his team seemed unmotivated and was affecting progress. Arthur suggested understanding what drives each team member individually and having one-on-one conversations. Harold admitted he had focused on goals/deadlines rather than personal motivations, said he would try Arthur’s suggestion, and felt more hopeful.
- Afterward, Harold felt hopeful and relieved. He believed Arthur’s advice would help and decided to implement it in team meetings. He told his team he wanted one-on-one chats to understand their motivations. He heard Team Member 1 say it could be helpful and Team Member 2 say they were open to it. Harold said he would schedule time with each of them and work toward project success together.
- Harold implemented the advice but noticed the team still was not responding well. He felt disappointed and worried about the project’s future and discussed it with Arthur again.
- Harold told Arthur the team still was not responding well. Arthur said there might be deeper issues, such as personal conflicts, lack of trust, or external stressors, and that Harold might need to dig deeper. Harold said he would set up another round of meetings to get to the bottom of it and thanked Arthur.
- Harold became determined and focused, believing there might be underlying team issues he had not addressed. He held one-on-one meetings to investigate team dynamics. He heard Team Member 1 say there was tension between a few team members affecting work. He heard Team Member 2 say they felt overwhelmed by the workload and had trouble staying motivated under stress. Harold said he would look into resolving conflicts and consider redistributing tasks, and that their well-being was important.
- Harold felt optimistic and empowered, believing that addressing individual concerns would improve team performance. He intended to create a more supportive, open environment through regular feedback sessions and team-building activities.
- Harold told the team he had heard their concerns and would make changes: regular feedback sessions and team-building activities. He heard Team Member 1 say that sounded great and would help them work better together, and Team Member 2 agree that it was good their concerns were being addressed. Harold said he was glad, urged them to work together for project success, and said their input and well-being were crucial.
